22.0.0.en: 1 And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his stead: for the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned. 2 Forty and two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Athaliah the daughter of Omri.

22.0.1.en: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his stead: for the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest.

22.0.2.en: So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned. [1]

22.0.3.en: From the words “the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah…” we infer that the inhabitants of Jerusalem were probably not content with his taking the throne, perhaps because he was the youngest of his brothers or because of the weakness of his character, but they had no alternative, since the Arabians had slain all his brothers.

22.0.4.en: He became king only in outward form, for it was his mother who managed the affairs of the kingdom.

22.1.0.en: Forty and two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Athaliah the daughter of Omri. [2]

22.1.1.en: The Septuagint says that Ahaziah’s age when he began to reign was twenty years. This is acceptable in light of what was said in the previous chapter, that Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he began to reign and reigned eight years, that is, he died at the age of forty; thus his son, who was twenty years old, had been born when his father was twenty. Ahaziah was influenced by the counsellors from the northern kingdom (Israel) more than any other king of Judah.

22.1.2.en: We read in the previous chapter of the captivity of the sons of Jehoram and his wives, but it did not say all his sons and all his wives. Therefore this chapter mentions one of his sons, “Ahaziah,” and one of his wives, “Athaliah,” who, together with her mother, the wicked Jezebel, may be said to have been a source of shame and disaster both for the kingdom of Israel and for the kingdom of Judah.

22.1.3.en: We have already seen how Athaliah wanted to destroy all the royal seed, in order to make sure that the divine promise concerning the continuance of David’s throne would not be fulfilled.

22.2.s.en: 2. Ahaziah walks in the way of Ahab

22.2.0.en: 3 He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly. 4 Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the LORD like the house of Ahab: for they were his counsellors after the death of his father to his destruction.

22.2.1.en: He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly. [3]

22.2.2.en: After the burial of his wicked father Jehoram, the people were perhaps expecting the youngest son not to walk as his father had, but his mother and his family drove him to walk in the very same way as his father.

22.2.3.en: Ahaziah had no principles by which to live, but he trusted in his mother Athaliah the daughter of Omri, a woman of great ambition and extreme violence, who led him and counselled him to do evil.

22.2.4.en: Ahaziah made an alliance with Jehoram the son of Ahab.

22.3.0.en: Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the LORD like the house of Ahab: for they were his counsellors after the death of his father to his destruction. [4]

22.4.s.en: 3. Ahaziah joins Jehoram in the war

22.4.0.en: He walked also after their counsel, and went with Jehoram the son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramothgilead: and the Syrians smote Joram. [5]

22.5.0.en: 6 And he returned to be healed in Jezreel because of the wounds which were given him at Ramah, when he fought with Hazael king of Syria. And Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram the son of Ahab at Jezreel, because he was sick. 7 And the destruction of Ahaziah was of God by coming to Joram: for when he was come, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab. 8 And it came to pass, that, when Jehu was executing judgment upon the house of Ahab, and found the princes of Judah, and the sons of the brethren of Ahaziah, that ministered to Ahaziah, he slew them. 9 And he sought Ahaziah: and they caught him, (for he was hid in Samaria,) and brought him to Jehu: and when they had slain him, they buried him: Because, said they, he is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart. So the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep still the kingdom.

22.5.1.en: And he returned to be healed in Jezreel because of the wounds which were given him at Ramah, when he fought with Hazael king of Syria.

22.5.2.en: And Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram the son of Ahab at Jezreel, because he was sick. [6]

22.6.0.en: And the destruction of Ahaziah was of God by coming to Joram.

22.6.1.en: For when he was come, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab. [7]

22.6.2.en: We have previously spoken of Jehu in our commentary on the Second Book of Kings (2 Kgs 9:27-28).

22.6.3.en: What happened to Ahaziah is the fruit of clinging to evil friendships, associating with the wicked and intermarrying with them, and also of his worship of idols. If we do not fear being infected by turning aside to evil, then let us fear perishing with the wicked. Therefore the commandment came: [Come out of Babylon] (Rev 18:4).

22.7.0.en: And it came to pass, that, when Jehu was executing judgment upon the house of Ahab, and found the princes of Judah, and the sons of the brethren of Ahaziah, that ministered to Ahaziah, he slew them. [8]

22.8.0.en: And he sought Ahaziah: and they caught him, (for he was hid in Samaria,) and brought him to Jehu: and when they had slain him, they buried him: Because, said they, he is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart.

22.8.1.en: So the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep still the kingdom. [9]

22.8.2.en: Jehu killed Ahaziah, who had hidden in Samaria, thinking that he would be safe, and Jehu left Ahaziah’s body to be buried.

22.9.s.en: 5. Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, seizes the throne

22.9.0.en: But when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah. [10]

22.9.1.en: This is recorded in (2 Kgs 11:1 etc.). Athaliah ordered the killing of her grandchildren in order to secure her remaining on the throne.

22.9.2.en: Athaliah was a wicked woman who sought to destroy the house of David forever, in order to set up a throne for herself on its ruins. She destroyed all the royal seed with brutality, and she probably wished to transfer the throne from the house of David to her relatives on her mother’s side.

22.9.3.en: The Holy Bible does not reveal her hidden motives and her plan, other than her securing that the throne would remain in her hand. The first to reflect on this matter was the historian Josephus, who described her actions as having inherited from her parents hatred for the house of David. He says of her that she wished “that no one of the house of David should remain alive, but that she should destroy the whole family, so that no king should afterwards take over afterwards, arising from the family [1].” Her motive was to prove false the divine promise that the seed of David would sit on the throne, and that the Messiah the Saviour would come from the seed of David.

22.9.4.en: Some see that, besides her desire that no one should touch her crown and that no one of the house of David should sit on the throne of Judah, Athaliah wanted to avenge the killing of Jezebel her mother and the destruction of her family at the hand of Jehu. She thought she was right to avenge her parents and her whole family even upon her own descendants, who were the successors of Jehoram of the house of David. Perhaps Athaliah had in the depths of her heart a bitter hatred for what had befallen her family; and her hatred for the house of David drove her to hate the God of David.

22.9.5.en: What Athaliah did was also practiced by Herod in the massacre of the children of Bethlehem, to keep the seat of the throne. Athaliah, and Herod also, thought that they had become secure, and did not realize that God is the Almighty and the Shepherd of His people.

22.9.6.en: God permitted what happened to the house of David to confirm that God’s care alone saved the situation, so that a small child of the house of David might remain, through whom a shining lamp would remain for the house, and from the seed of David the Messiah the Saviour would come. In vain the enemy of good tried to nullify God’s plan of salvation.

22.9.7.en: v I observed the wicked, and I saw them in peace. What peace? A temporary peace, changing, passing and earthly; and yet I also ask this of God. I saw those who did not serve God receiving what I desired, I who serve God, but my feet were almost gone, my steps had well nigh slipped (Ps 73:2). Now I understand why they have peace and refreshment on earth… because their punishment is not temporary, but fixed forever [2].

22.9.8.en: St. Augustine v Of the wicked after their death it is said: “Where is the tabernacle of the dwellingplaces of the wicked?”

22.9.9.en: If you consider this closely, can you deny that there is recompense from the divine justice? Happiness floods the heart of the first (the righteous), and misery the second. The first bears witness by his own soul that he is innocent of guilt, and the second is a criminal.

22.9.10.en: That man is happy in his departure from the world, and the other is grieved over.

22.9.11.en: Who can pronounce innocent one who is not innocent in the eyes of his own conscience? He says: [Where is the covering of his tent, his memorial shall not be found] (cf. Job 28:21).

22.9.12.en: The life of the criminal is a dream. No, even the very rest of the wicked while they live here is an illusion; they are in hell now, since they go down into Gehenna while they are alive [3].

22.9.13.en: v St. Job answers: Do not think that you are happy while you are immersed in pleasures, because the blows of God have not fallen upon you in this life.

22.9.14.en: “The lamp of the wicked is put out.” It gives light for a time, but it does not carry an eternal light.

22.9.15.en: And although the world favors such people, because they carry out the will of God who has authority over the world (Jn 14:30), yet usually a moment of reversal in events comes, when sorrows come from the wrath and indignation of heaven, when the wicked are sifted “as stubble before the wind.” The unjust are sifted like chaff, and the righteous like wheat. Turn to the Lord who said to Peter: “Behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not” (Lk 22:31-32) [4].

22.9.16.en: St. Ambrose v “And the number of the years of his oppression is uncertain”… It is known that every proud man exercises tyranny according to his measure. One exercises it in a state, by virtue of his high position that suits him; another in a province, another in a city, another in his household, and another hides his evil and exercises it upon himself in the thought of his heart.

22.9.17.en: For God is not concerned with the quantity of evil that a man is able to practice, but with the quantity that is in his mind to practice. And when a man has no authority outwardly, he is counted a tyrant inwardly, and iniquity rules over him within. For although he does not oppress his relatives outwardly, inwardly he seeks to find an opportunity and authority to oppress others. For God looks into the hearts of men, and in the eyes of God the wicked man is counted as having actually done what he imagines.

22.10.s.en: 6. Joash the son of Ahaziah hidden in the temple

22.10.0.en: 11 But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king’s sons that were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, (for she was the sister of Ahaziah,) hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not. 12 And he was with them hid in the house of God six years: and Athaliah reigned over the land.

22.10.1.en: But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king’s sons that were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest,

22.10.2.en: (for she was the sister of Ahaziah,)

22.10.3.en: hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not. [11]

22.10.4.en: Ahaziah trusted in his mother Athaliah the daughter of Omri, an extremely violent woman, who counselled him to do evil [3]. He made an alliance with Jehoram the son of Ahab.

22.10.5.en: In the midst of the massacre that Athaliah carried out to destroy all the royal seed so that she alone might remain in power, the lamp of the Lord’s anointed was not put out; for God preserved a weak infant, as a symbol of the Lord Christ, who was preserved from the massacre of the children of Bethlehem.

22.10.6.en: In the sabbatical year, the seventh year, the year of the land’s rest, Joash appeared to reign before the eyes of all; it was declared that he was the only king who had the authority to wear the crown.

22.10.7.en: v Just as what God has prepared for those who love Him surpasses the mind, so also the torments He has prepared for the wicked surpass the mind [5].

22.10.8.en: Origen v The wicked are scattered bitterly (like light tares), but the righteous are saved like heavy wheat. Notice what the Lord says to Peter: “Behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not” (Lk 22:31-32). Those who are scattered like tares perish, but he who does not perish is like the seed that falls and grows and increases and brings forth much fruit (Lk 8:8)… Evil is likened to the chaff that burns quickly and turns to dust [6].

22.11.0.en: And he was with them hid in the house of God six years: and Athaliah reigned over the land. [12]

22.11.1.en: Her love of shedding blood made her lose her popularity, if she ever had any. Her taking the throne had no legal basis whatever. All that characterized her was her violence and tyranny, and she thought that no one could disobey her or resist her.

22.11.2.en: The hiding of the child in the house of God came by surpassing divine wisdom: 1. It was not possible for any man to hide the child in his house, lest the news leak out and Athaliah take vengeance on the owner of the house and all his family. 2. The remaining of a little child with his nurse in the house of the Lord for six years without the news leaking out to the queen did not happen in vain, but by a divine plan that reveals God’s own care for the matter. 3. The keeping of the child in the house of the Lord under the care of the high priest revealed the plan of God, who assigned a certain tribe to the priestly work and another to the kingly work, with the cooperation of the two tribes. It is as though God declares His care for His people spiritually and temporally.

22.11.3.en: Grant me the spirit of care and leadership

22.11.4.en: v Grant me Your Spirit working in me, O Good Shepherd.

22.11.5.en: In Your love You shepherd Your people, and You lay down Yourself for them.

22.11.6.en: In Your love You raise up from every child a loving leader!

22.11.7.en: v Ahaziah took the throne, and he had no sincere principles.

22.11.8.en: His wicked mother led him and counselled him with her evil.

22.11.9.en: She drove him to evil, and deprived him of clinging to You.

22.11.10.en: She drove him to cling to Jehoram the idolater.

22.11.11.en: He thought that in his alliance with Jehoram his soul would be at ease.

22.11.12.en: But behold, death pursued him, and shame clung to him.

22.11.13.en: v Athaliah, his mother, took the throne of her son.

22.11.14.en: In her love of power, she killed every male of the house of David.

22.11.15.en: She killed and rested, and thought that she was in safety and stability.

22.11.16.en: There was no longer anyone to rival her for her throne.

22.11.17.en: There was no one who could stand before her.

22.11.18.en: And in the whole kingdom there was no one who could disobey her.

22.11.19.en: She remained on the throne six years, and thought that she was mighty and wise and a unique leader.

22.11.20.en: No one of the house of David was sitting on the throne any longer.

22.11.21.en: And the prophecies concerning the house of David could not be fulfilled.

22.11.22.en: v But You, O Good Shepherd, rescued a child one year old.

22.11.23.en: You embraced him in Your holy temple.

22.11.24.en: You guarded him with Your care, and prepared him to sit on the throne.

22.11.25.en: You work through the many as through the few, and through the great as through the little child.

22.11.26.en: You pour out Your Spirit upon Your believers, and they bear the spirit of love, care and leadership!
